item.text: {"summary":"No safe production edit can be proposed from the supplied source excerpts.","explanation":"The assertions identify two failure groups. In ParseTime.Basics, parsing \"2013-06-28 19:08:09 -0800\" succeeds, but the expected CivilSecond(2013, 6, 28, 19, 8, 9) differs from ci.cs, which is 2013-06-28T03:08:09. In ParseTime.WithTimeZone, parsing \"2013-06-28 19:08:09 +0800\" succeeds, but the expected CivilSecond(2013, 6, 28, 19, 8, 9) differs from ci.cs, which is 2013-06-29T11:08:09. FormatParse.RoundTrip likewise expects in + subseconds and in to equal out; out is shifted from 18:08:07 to 04:08:07 while retaining the +02:00 suffix. These failures point to incorrect numeric-offset sign handling. ParseTime.ExtendedOffsetErrors expects ParseTime(\"%z\", \"-1\", &t, &err) and ParseTime(\"%Ez\", \"-1\", &t, &err) to return false with an error containing \"Failed to parse\"; both return true, and the displayed \"Illegal trailing data\" is the actual err value. The supplied format.cc delegates parsing to cctz::detail::parse, but the implementation of its numeric-offset parser is not included. Without that current implementation, proposing an exact, unique replacement anchor or a coherent correction would require guessing the missing implementation, which the instructions prohibit.","edits":[{"path":"absl/time/internal/cctz/src/time_zone_format.cc","old":" unavailable in supplied current source","new":""}]}
